newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sees explosive growth in electronic commerce.
newsitem.headline: EU sees explosive growth in electronic commerce.

text.p: Computer shopping and other electronic trade could bring in $100 billion a year by the year 2000 compared with only $4 billion now, a European Commission official said on Wednesday.

"So this is rapidly expanding and certainly Europe will have to be in the forefront here, which we are not yet," said Magnus Lemmel, deputy director general at the European Commission's industry department.
"What we are trying to achieve is a system which will certainly revolutionise our lives," he said.
Electronic trading involves a wide range of technologies, including buying and selling on the Internet, e-mail, fax, electronic data interchange and electronic payments.
Lemmel was briefing journalists on a Group of Seven (G7) most industrialised nations conference on the global marketplace for small and medium-sized companies (SMEs).
The European Commission is organising the April 7-9 meeting in Bonn.
"For SMEs...I think electronic commerce is particularly important because it could certainly facilitate life for SMEs and improve their market position," Lemmel said.
The conference will deal with topical issues such as security and legal and contractual matters. "Privacy, things like this, must be dealt with," Lemmel said.
He warned of the risk that if individual EU countries took their own initiatives in this field, "then we will not be able to build up a coherent electronic commerce system in Europe."
It was also vital to boost training and awareness of electronic commerce. -- Brussels newsroom +32 2 287 68 11
